fullPassage:
Stress not only affects physical disease but also the very structure of our brains, making us even more likely to experience a drained brain.

(C) A number of studies have been done to reveal what happens in healthy people's brains when they go through something stressful. One study demonstrated a link between a smaller hippocampus and people who had experienced long-lasting stress.

(A) Why does this matter? This part of the brain helps you remain resilient in the face of stress and is involved in mood regulation. It also helps you to monitor the safety of your environment and store dangerous images in your long-term memory so you can avoid them in the future.

(B) It does all these things as part of its duties of regulating your sympathetic and parasympathetic nervous systems. But chronic stress can confuse the hippocampus and lead to turning signals for cortisol 'on' instead of 'off,' which can trap you in a constant state of fight, flight, or freeze.

questions.passage: Stress not only affects physical (A)[disease / health] but also the very (B)[structure / destruction] of our brains, making us more likely to experience a (C)[drained / energized] brain. (C) A number of studies have been done to reveal what happens in healthy people's brains when they go through something stressful. One study demonstrated a link between a smaller hippocampus and people who had experienced long-lasting stress. (A) Why does this matter? This part of the brain helps you remain resilient in the face of stress and is involved in mood regulation. It also helps you to monitor the safety of your environment and store dangerous images in your long-term memory so you can avoid them in the future.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 스트레스는 신체 질병(disease)뿐 아니라 뇌의 구조(structure)에도 영향을 미쳐 소진된(drained) 뇌를 경험하게 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① disease — structure — drained: 원문과 일치
❌ ② health(건강): disease의 반의어
❌ ③ destruction(파괴): structure의 반의어
❌ ④ energized(활력있는): drained의 반의어

questions.passage: One study (A)[demonstrated / concealed] a link between a smaller hippocampus and people who had experienced (B)[long-lasting / brief] stress. This part of the brain helps you remain (C)[resilient / vulnerable] in the face of stress.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 한 연구가 해마 축소와 오래 지속된(long-lasting) 스트레스 경험자 간의 연관성을 보여주었다(demonstrated). 이 뇌 부분은 스트레스에 회복력(resilient)을 유지하게 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ demonstrated — long-lasting — resilient: 원문과 일치
❌ ① concealed(숨긴): demonstrated의 반의어
❌ ② brief(짧은): long-lasting의 반의어
❌ ④ vulnerable(취약한): resilient의 반의어

questions.passage: The hippocampus is involved in mood (A)[regulation / disruption]. Chronic stress can (B)[confuse / clarify] the hippocampus and lead to turning signals for cortisol 'on,' which can trap you in a (C)[constant / temporary] state of fight, flight, or freeze.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 해마는 기분 조절(regulation)에 관여한다. 만성 스트레스는 해마를 혼란시키고(confuse) 코르티솔 신호를 켜, 지속적인(constant) 투쟁/도주/경직 상태에 가둘 수 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② regulation — confuse — constant: 원문과 일치
❌ ① disruption(혼란): regulation의 반의어
❌ ③ clarify(명확히 하다): confuse의 반의어
❌ ④ temporary(일시적인): constant의 반의어

questions.passage: Stress not only affects physical disease but also the very structure of our brains. A number of studies have been done to ①<u>reveal</u> what happens in healthy people's brains. One study ②<u>demonstrated</u> a link between a smaller hippocampus and long-lasting stress. This part of the brain helps you remain ③<u>resilient</u> in the face of stress. Chronic stress can trap you in a ④<u>temporary</u> state of fight, flight, or freeze.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ temporary(일시적인) → constant(지속적인): 만성 스트레스로 인해 '지속적인' 상태에 갇힌다는 맥락.
det.analysis:
✅ ① reveal(밝히다): 원문 일치
✅ ② demonstrated(보여주었다): 원문 일치
✅ ③ resilient(회복력 있는): 원문 일치
❌ ④ temporary(일시적인): 원문은 constant(지속적인) — 반의어로 교체됨

questions.passage: This part of the brain helps you remain resilient and is involved in mood ①<u>regulation</u>. It helps you ②<u>monitor</u> the safety of your environment and store ③<u>dangerous</u> images in your long-term memory. Chronic stress can ④<u>assist</u> the hippocampus and lead to turning signals for cortisol 'on.'
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ assist(돕다) → confuse(혼란시키다): 만성 스트레스는 해마를 '혼란시킨다'는 맥락.
det.analysis:
✅ ① regulation(조절): 원문 일치
✅ ② monitor(감시하다): 원문 일치
✅ ③ dangerous(위험한): 원문 일치
❌ ④ assist(돕다): 원문은 confuse(혼란시키다) — 반의어로 교체됨

questions.passage: A number of studies have been done to reveal what happens in healthy people's brains when they go through something ①<u>stressful</u>. One study demonstrated a link between a ②<u>larger</u> hippocampus and people who had experienced long-lasting stress. It also helps you to ③<u>monitor</u> the safety of your environment. Chronic stress can lead to turning signals for cortisol 'on' instead of ④<u>'off.'</u>
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ② larger(더 큰) → smaller(더 작은): 오래 지속된 스트레스를 겪은 사람은 해마가 '더 작다'는 연구 결과.
det.analysis:
✅ ① stressful(스트레스를 주는): 원문 일치
❌ ② larger(더 큰): 원문은 smaller(더 작은) — 반의어로 교체됨
✅ ③ monitor(감시하다): 원문 일치
✅ ④ 'off'(끄기): 원문 일치
det.tip: smaller hippocampus ↔ larger hippocampus — 스트레스가 해마를 축소시킨다

questions.passage: One study demonstrated a link between a smaller hippocampus and people who had experienced long-lasting stress. (A) Why does this matter? This part of the brain helps you remain __________ in the face of stress and is involved in mood regulation. It also helps you to monitor the safety of your environment and store dangerous images in your long-term memory so you can avoid them in the future. (B) It does all these things as part of its duties of regulating your sympathetic and parasympathetic nervous systems.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 이 뇌 부분은 스트레스에 회복력 있는(resilient) 상태를 유지하도록 돕는다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① resilient(회복력 있는): 스트레스에 대한 저항력
❌ ② anxious(불안한): 스트레스 유발 의미
❌ ③ passive(수동적인): 회복력과 무관
❌ ④ indifferent(무관심한): 문맥과 부적절
det.tip: resilient = 회복력 있는, 탄력 있는 — in the face of stress

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 한 연구가 더 작은 해마(hippocampus)와 장기 스트레스 경험자 간의 연관성을 보여주었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ hippocampus(해마): 글의 핵심 뇌 부위
❌ ① cerebellum(소뇌): 운동 조절 부위
❌ ② amygdala(편도체): 감정 관련이지만 원문은 hippocampus
❌ ④ cortex(피질): 뇌 표면 부위
det.tip: hippocampus(해마): 기억, 감정 조절, 스트레스 반응에 관여하는 뇌 부위

questions.passage: But __________ stress can confuse the hippocampus and lead to turning signals for cortisol 'on' instead of 'off,' which can trap you in a constant state of fight, flight, or freeze.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 만성(chronic) 스트레스가 해마를 혼란시키고 코르티솔 신호를 켜 놓을 수 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② chronic(만성의): 지속적 스트레스가 해마에 영향
❌ ① acute(급성의): 단기적 스트레스
❌ ③ mild(가벼운): 심각도가 낮음
❌ ④ occasional(가끔의): 빈도가 낮음
det.tip: chronic(만성의) ↔ acute(급성의) — chronic stress = 만성 스트레스

questions.passage: Stress not only affects physical disease but also the very structure of our brains, making us even more likely to experience a drained brain. (C) A number of studies have been done to reveal what <u>happens</u> in healthy people's brains when they go through something stressful. One study demonstrated a link between a smaller hippocampus and people who had experienced long-lasting stress. (A) Why does this matter?
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>reveal</u>과 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: reveal = 밝히다, 드러내다
det.analysis:
✅ ② uncover(밝히다): reveal과 동의어
❌ ① conceal(숨기다): 반의어
❌ ③ ignore(무시하다): 의미 다름
❌ ④ assume(가정하다): 의미 다름

questions.passage: (C) A number of studies have been done to reveal what happens in healthy people's brains when they go through something stressful. One study demonstrated a link between a <u>smaller</u> hippocampus and people who had experienced long-lasting stress. (A) Why does this matter? This part of the brain helps you remain resilient in the face of stress and is involved in mood regulation.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>demonstrated</u>와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: demonstrated = 보여주었다, 입증했다
det.analysis:
✅ ④ showed(보여주었다): demonstrated와 동의어
❌ ① refuted(반박했다): 반의어
❌ ② questioned(의문시했다): 의미 다름
❌ ③ overlooked(간과했다): 의미 다름

questions.passage: This part of the brain helps you remain resilient in the face of stress and is involved in mood regulation. It also helps you to monitor the safety of your <u>environment</u> and store dangerous images in your long-term memory so you can avoid them in the future. (B) It does all these things as part of its duties of regulating your sympathetic and parasympathetic nervous systems. But chronic stress can confuse the hippocampus and lead to turning signals for cortisol 'on' instead of 'off,' which can trap you in a constant state of fight, flight, or freeze.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>monitor</u>와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: monitor = 감시하다, 관찰하다
det.analysis:
✅ ③ observe(관찰하다): monitor와 동의어
❌ ① ignore(무시하다): 반의어
❌ ② manipulate(조작하다): 의미 다름
❌ ④ control(통제하다): 감시와 통제는 다름
det.tip: monitor = observe = watch over = 감시하다, 관찰하다

questions.passage: Stress not only affects physical disease but also the very structure of our brains, making us even more likely to experience a drained brain. (C) A number of studies have been done to reveal what happens in healthy people's brains when they go through something stressful. One study demonstrated a link between a <u>smaller</u> hippocampus and people who had experienced long-lasting stress. (A) Why does this matter? questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>resilient</u>의 반의어로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: resilient(회복력 있는)의 반의어 = fragile(취약한)
det.analysis:
✅ ③ fragile(취약한): resilient의 반의어
❌ ① tough(강인한): 유의어
❌ ② robust(튼튼한): 유의어
❌ ④ durable(내구성 있는): 유의어

questions.passage: (C) A number of studies have been done to reveal what happens in healthy people's brains when they go through something stressful. One study demonstrated a link between a smaller <u>hippocampus</u> and people who had experienced long-lasting stress. (A) Why does this matter? This part of the brain helps you remain resilient in the face of stress and is involved in mood regulation.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>chronic</u>의 반의어로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: chronic(만성의)의 반의어 = acute(급성의)
det.analysis:
✅ ① acute(급성의): chronic의 반의어
❌ ② persistent(지속적인): 유의어
❌ ③ recurring(반복되는): 유의어에 가까움
❌ ④ prolonged(장기적인): 유의어
det.tip: chronic(만성의) ↔ acute(급성의) — chronic = 오래 지속되는, acute = 짧고 급격한

questions.passage: This part of the brain helps you remain resilient in the face of stress and is involved in mood regulation. It also helps you to monitor the safety of your environment and store dangerous images in your long-term memory so you can avoid them in the future. It does all these things as part of its <u>duties</u> of regulating your sympathetic and parasympathetic nervous systems. But chronic stress can confuse the hippocampus and lead to turning signals for cortisol 'on' instead of 'off,' which can trap you in a constant state of fight, flight, or freeze.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>regulating</u>이 이 글에서 의미하는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: regulating = 조절하는, 통제하는 (신경 시스템을 조절)
det.analysis:
✅ ② controlling(통제하는): 신경 시스템을 조절한다는 맥락
❌ ① creating(만드는): 신경을 만드는 것이 아님
❌ ③ damaging(손상시키는): 부정적 의미
❌ ④ measuring(측정하는): 측정이 아닌 조절

questions.stem:
다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?
"a hormone released in response to stress that prepares the body for a 'fight or flight' reaction"

det.korean: 스트레스 반응으로 분비되어 '투쟁 또는 도주' 반응을 준비시키는 호르몬 = cortisol(코르티솔)
det.analysis:
✅ ③ cortisol(코르티솔): 스트레스 호르몬
❌ ① serotonin(세로토닌): 행복 호르몬
❌ ② dopamine(도파민): 보상 호르몬
❌ ④ insulin(인슐린): 혈당 조절 호르몬
det.tip: cortisol = 코르티솔, 스트레스 호르몬 — fight, flight, or freeze 반응과 관련

questions.passage: (A) Why does this matter? __________ It also helps you to monitor the safety of your environment and store dangerous images in your long-term memory so you can avoid them in the future. (B) It does all these things as part of its duties of regulating your sympathetic and parasympathetic nervous systems.
questions.stem:
다음 괄호 안의 단어를 문맥에 맞게 변형하시오.
"This part of the brain is involved in mood (regulate)."

det.korean: regulate → regulation: 명사형으로 변환. mood regulation = 기분 조절.
det.analysis: regulate(동사: 조절하다) → regulation(명사: 조절). mood 뒤에 명사가 와야 함.

questions.passage: (C) A number of studies have been done to reveal what happens in healthy people's brains when they go through something stressful. __________ (A) Why does this matter? This part of the brain helps you remain resilient in the face of stress and is involved in mood regulation.
questions.stem:
다음 괄호 안의 단어를 문맥에 맞게 변형하시오.
"One study (demonstration) a link between a smaller hippocampus and long-lasting stress."

det.korean: demonstration → demonstrated: 과거 동사형으로 변환. 연구가 보여주었다는 과거 사실.
det.analysis: demonstration(명사: 시연) → demonstrated(동사 과거: 보여주었다). 주어 One study의 동사 필요.

questions.passage: Stress not only affects physical disease but also the very structure of our brains, making us even more likely to experience a __________ brain. questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 스트레스는 소진된(drained) 뇌를 경험하게 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② drained(소진된): 스트레스로 에너지가 빠진 뇌
❌ ① refreshed(상쾌한): 스트레스와 반대
❌ ③ active(활발한): 긍정적 의미
❌ ④ sharp(날카로운): 긍정적 의미
det.tip: drained = 소진된, 기진맥진한 — 스트레스의 부정적 결과

questions.passage: This part of the brain helps you remain resilient in the face of stress and is involved in mood regulation. It also helps you to monitor the safety of your environment and store dangerous images in your long-term memory so you can avoid them in the future. It does all these things as part of its duties of regulating your sympathetic and __________ nervous systems. But chronic stress can confuse the hippocampus.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 교감신경계와 부교감(parasympathetic) 신경계를 조절하는 것이 해마의 역할이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ parasympathetic(부교감의): sympathetic과 짝을 이루는 신경계
❌ ① peripheral(말초의): 교감/부교감과 다른 분류
❌ ② central(중추의): 교감/부교감과 다른 분류
❌ ③ autonomous(자율의): autonomic이 정확한 표현
